source-integrity.provenance: Primary Q2 2026 SEC filing and issuer contract/mission disclosures, SEC registration-review evidence, independent financial analysis, and current independent market valuation; overlapping issuer claims collapsed by origin.
source-integrity.freshness: Operating evidence through Q2 2026; independent market valuation as of 2026-09-30.
source-integrity.duplicateOriginCollapse: Issuer Q2 metrics and SEC-filed company metrics are treated as the same underlying company-origin facts where overlapping; SEC staff comment evidence is retained as a distinct regulatory origin; independent financial and market-data sources are distinct.
source-integrity.sourceIndependence: Independent financial analysis and S&P Global-derived current market data constrain company-reported growth; mission reliability, margin conversion and customer concentration remain important unknowns.

company-underwriting.operatingTrajectory: First-half 2026 revenue expanded sharply and backlog/deferred revenue support demand, but operating cash outflow increased materially and free cash flow remains deeply negative.
company-underwriting.contractsBacklogCustomers: Lockheed Martin multi-launch demand, NASA CLPS work and approximately $1.5B backlog support visibility, while government/program concentration and mission scheduling remain material.
company-underwriting.balanceSheetRunwayDebtDilution: Q2 liquidity was substantial, but continuing negative cash generation and the large increase in shares outstanding after the IPO make dilution-adjusted economics a central constraint.
company-underwriting.governanceCapitalAllocation: Management is funding simultaneous launch, lunar/spacecraft and Eclipse development; the SEC filing supports the capital-allocation burden, but evidence does not justify a strong stewardship band absent longer public-market execution history.
company-underwriting.pricingPowerConcentration: Mission complexity and contracted demand support some value capture, but durable margin/pricing evidence is not yet established and government/customer concentration limits confidence.
company-underwriting.catalystsRisks: Backlog conversion, repeatable Alpha Block II cadence, Eclipse development and upcoming earnings are catalysts; launch failure, FAA/regulatory interruption, cash burn and dilution are key risks.

thesisQuality.basis: Rapid revenue growth, roughly $1.5B backlog and major launch/lunar contracts demonstrate real demand, while cadence reliability and cash economics remain unproven.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Revenue and backlog expanded strongly, but first-half operating cash outflow rose to $144.1M and independent analysis reports Q2 free cash flow of negative $106.31M.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: At 2026-09-30 the company carried about $3.88B market capitalization and $3.29B enterprise value, roughly 13.5x trailing sales, despite negative earnings/free cash flow and major execution risk.

catalystScore.basis: Backlog conversion, repeat Alpha Block II missions, Eclipse development and the next earnings checkpoint are identifiable material catalysts, but timing remains mission-dependent.

governancePower.basis: Management has secured capital and major contracts, but simultaneous capital-intensive programs, negative cash generation and limited public-market execution history keep governance/capital-allocation evidence mixed.

alignment2036.basis: Responsive launch, lunar delivery and spacecraft infrastructure address durable civil, defense and commercial space-access needs.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Launch, lunar/spacecraft and medium-lift development reuse propulsion, flight and mission capabilities across distinct civil, defense and commercial demand engines.

bottleneckControl.basis: Launch capacity and mission integration are real constraints with qualification friction, but Firefly does not yet demonstrate dominant scarce capacity or irreplaceability.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Multiple customer/program channels diversify demand, but launch reliability, regulatory continuity and capital intensity create a narrow execution dependency across scenarios.

substitutionResilience.basis: Flight heritage, integrated mission capability and contracted customers create moderate replacement barriers, while alternative launch providers remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.basis: The filing identifies production and launch-rate execution dependencies; current evidence does not establish exceptional multi-source redundancy or tested resilience.

pricingPower.basis: Large mission contracts support some value capture, but current evidence does not establish durable price pass-through or margin-protected scarcity rents.

riskEvidence.basis: Launch reliability and FAA interruption can directly impair contracted-demand conversion; operating cash burn is high, simultaneous programs are capital intensive, and current valuation embeds substantial execution expectations.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Fresh SEC operating/risk evidence, SEC regulatory-review evidence, issuer contract disclosures, independent financial analysis and current S&P Global-derived market valuation cover the major score dimensions; confidence remains below exceptional because long-cycle launch cadence, customer concentration, margin conversion and supply-chain redundancy remain incompletely observed.

scoreRecord.thesis: Firefly has credible demand across responsive launch, lunar and spacecraft missions, but durable shareholder value depends on converting backlog into reliable mission cadence and improving cash economics faster than capital needs and dilution compound.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: A launch failure or regulatory interruption can delay revenue and damage customer confidence while high cash burn and simultaneous development programs increase financing and dilution risk.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Repeatable Alpha Block II mission success and backlog conversion, followed by the November 2026 earnings checkpoint and evidence of improving operating/free-cash-flow burden.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Revenue and backlog expanded strongly, but first-half operating cash outflow rose materially and free cash flow remains deeply negative.

riskEvidence.basis: Launch/regulatory interruption, cash burn, capital intensity and demanding valuation remain material.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Multiple primary/regulatory and independent source classes constrain the underwriting; important forward execution unknowns remain.
